target: ADR-002 Package and workspace layout (proposed by hsdd/spec/nidana.md)

decisions.question: What slug does the ADR file take?

options.label: 002-package-workspace-layout
options.consequence: Three-word kebab slug naming both halves of the topic, within hsdd-adr's 2 to 4 words.

options.label: 002-package-and-workspace-layout
options.consequence: Mirrors the title word for word; five words, over hsdd-adr's slug length.

options.label: 002-pub-workspace
options.consequence: Shorter, but drops the package set, which is half of the decision.

decisions.chosen: 002-package-workspace-layout
decisions.why: hsdd-adr asks for a 2 to 4 word kebab slug of the decision topic; this one keeps both the package set and the workspace. Naming only, no evidence needed.

decisions.question: Does the package set and naming of the root's proposal hold on the pinned SDK (eight members under packages/, Guide B.2 names where a package keeps its layer's role, layers 2 and 3 folded into nidana_dart_runtime, no rxdart adapter, persistence, perf-suite, devtools or test-utilities package)?

options.label: Keep the proposal's package set and names
options.consequence: Eight members, traceable to Guide B.2; the experiment builds and tests a stand-in of exactly this set in one workspace with a Flutter member.

options.label: Guide B.2 exactly
options.consequence: Adds nidana_dart_runtime_rxdart and a test-utilities package: an engine abstraction with one implementation and a package that cannot be tested apart from the runtime.

options.label: Add a separate scan or checks package
options.consequence: A ninth package with a clearer name for the aggregate checks; the scan would then share the topology catalog scan with the codegen across a package boundary.

decisions.chosen: Keep the proposal's package set and names
decisions.why: The stand-in workspace (wl_* for nidana_*) resolves, analyzes, tests and runs build_runner with this exact set on Flutter 3.47.7 / Dart 3.13.5. The fold of layers 2 and 3 and the absence of a test-utilities package rest on root D3 and D4 (RxDart is the only engine, TestBus cannot be tested apart from the runtime). The reasons root S02 marked for upstreaming (Guide B.2 omits the test-utilities and telemetry packages) still hold. Signal that would split the runtime: a v1 requirement for a second engine.

decisions.question: Does the analysis server plugin stay the static-analysis mechanism once the real single resolution is known (the proposal's rationale said that without custom_lint 'the SDK's analyzer 14.5.0 resolves')?

options.label: Analysis server plugin, no custom_lint
options.consequence: Rules run under dart analyze and the IDE; the workspace resolves analyzer 13.3.0, the best a resolution holding Flutter and test can reach.

options.label: custom_lint as Spec §3.11 and Guide C.2 name
options.consequence: Matches the text, but custom_lint 0.8.1 requires analyzer ^8.0.0 and would hold the whole workspace at 8.4.0.

options.label: custom_lint in a package outside the workspace
options.consequence: Keeps the workspace current, but the lint package resolves apart from what it checks and from the codegen.

decisions.chosen: Analysis server plugin, no custom_lint
decisions.why: The proposal's claim of analyzer 14.5.0 was measured without Flutter. With Flutter and test in the same resolution, flutter_test's test_api 0.7.12 pin holds test at 1.31.1, whose test_core caps analyzer below 14, so the workspace gets 13.3.0 (Q1, Q2). The comparison still favors the plugin: 13.3.0 against custom_lint's 8.4.0, which pub.dev's custom_lint 0.8.1 (analyzer ^8.0.0) forces. Corrected in the ADR's Context and in OQ9's detail. Marked for upstreaming: Spec §3.11 and Guide C.2 name custom_lint.

decisions.question: What does the root analysis_options.yaml contain beyond the proposal's excludes?

options.label: lints/recommended plus strict-casts, strict-inference, strict-raw-types
options.consequence: Every member inherits one lint set and the strict modes ADR-001's surface fixtures use; a member surface that leaks dynamic fails its own analyze before it fails a surface replay. The root gains lints as its only dev dependency.

options.label: Excludes only
options.consequence: No shared lint set; implementation_imports and depend_on_referenced_packages go unchecked, and a dynamic leak shows only at the surface replay.

options.label: flutter_lints for every member
options.consequence: Adds Flutter-specific rules to pure Dart packages and a Flutter package to the root's dev dependencies.

decisions.chosen: lints/recommended plus strict-casts, strict-inference, strict-raw-types
decisions.why: The experiment shows members without an options file inherit the root's lint set and strict modes, and the recommended set's implementation_imports enforces the proposal's 'public libraries only' rule (Q11). ADR-001 analyzes surface fixtures under the same strict modes, so code and fixtures agree. lints 6.1.0 resolves beside Flutter. Signal that would change it: Flutter-specific rules wanted in nidana_dart_runtime_flutter, which a member options file that includes the root's can add.

decisions.question: ADR-001 follow-up: does the root's exclude list add hsdd/** beside ref/** and docs/**?

options.label: Exclude ref/**, docs/** and hsdd/**
options.consequence: Workspace-wide analysis never reports a fixture's deliberate errors; the replay tool analyzes fixtures by explicit path.

options.label: Rely on the nested fixture options file only
options.consequence: Reject fixtures' deliberate errors would fail every workspace-wide analyze.

decisions.chosen: Exclude ref/**, docs/** and hsdd/**
decisions.why: ADR-001 Decision item 2 and its Consequences require it, and its experiment shows the exclude hides fixtures from a workspace-wide analyze while explicit paths still analyze. This experiment adds that the excludes also hide a nested package under docs/ whose options name a nonexistent plugin (Q11), and that ADR-001's nested fixture options keep the root-enabled plugin off fixtures (Q11d). ref/ holds no Dart file today; its exclude is free.

decisions.question: Does the root workspace: list name members explicitly or by glob?

options.label: Explicit member list
options.consequence: Every member is added deliberately by the phase that creates it, matching 'one owning node per package'; the root pubspec.yaml changes with each new member.

options.label: Glob packages/*
options.consequence: The root pubspec never changes, but any directory under packages/ joins the resolution without an owner.

decisions.chosen: Explicit member list
decisions.why: Globs work on the pinned SDK (Q4; Dart 3.11+ per the pub workspaces page), so the choice is not forced. An explicit list makes membership a reviewed change and keeps a stray directory out of the single resolution. Cost: phases that create members edit the same file, which phase planning must serialize with Collides with. Signal that would change it: many parallel member-creating phases colliding on the root pubspec.

decisions.question: How do members declare dependencies on each other: hosted version constraints or path dependencies?

options.label: Hosted version constraints
options.consequence: The workspace resolves them to the local member and the member stays publishable unchanged; outside the workspace they resolve against pub.dev, so consumers before publication need overrides.

options.label: Path dependencies
options.consequence: Resolve inside and outside the workspace, but every publishable member then fails dart analyze with invalid_dependency and fails pub publish.

decisions.chosen: Hosted version constraints
decisions.why: A hosted constraint resolves to the local member, and a version mismatch fails resolution loudly (Q3); a member with hosted sibling constraints passes publish validation except for metadata (Q16); a path dependency in a publishable package is an analyzer warning that fails the root analyze and a publish error (Q11, Q16). The pub workspaces page shows the same form.

decisions.question: How are third-party version constraints written across members that share one resolution?

options.label: Caret on the locked version, same constraint in every member
options.consequence: The lower bound is a version the lockfile actually tested, and members never disagree on a package's range.

options.label: Each member chooses its own constraints
options.consequence: Less coordination, but lower bounds below the locked version go untested and ranges drift between members.

options.label: any everywhere
options.consequence: No bookkeeping, but published packages carry no meaningful bounds and pub warns at publish.

decisions.chosen: Caret on the locked version, same constraint in every member
decisions.why: One lockfile tests one version of each package, so only a lower bound equal to that version is tested; pub publish validation also asks for real constraints (Q16 shows the warning for unconstrained dependencies). Judgement beyond that; no experiment compares the alternatives. Signal that would change it: a published release that must support adopters on older dependency versions, which would need a pub downgrade gate.

decisions.question: Where do example/ folders go: non-member packages with uncommitted lockfiles (the proposal), nested workspace members, or plain folders inside their member with no pubspec?

options.label: No pubspec: part of the member
options.consequence: An example analyzes with its member and uses its dependencies; no extra resolution; the runnable example app stays nidana_integration.

options.label: Non-member example packages
options.consequence: The root pub get also resolves each member's example/ outside the workspace, where an unpublished sibling cannot be found, so it fails with exit 69.

options.label: Nested workspace members
options.consequence: Works, but each example adds a package to the single resolution and its pubspec ships in the parent's archive.

decisions.chosen: No pubspec: part of the member
decisions.why: The proposal's option breaks the root pub get on the pinned SDK (Q6a): pub get resolves example/ folders by default, outside the workspace. Nested members work (Q6b) but buy nothing nidana_integration does not already provide. A pubspec-free example analyzes and runs as part of its member (Q6c). This changes the proposal's item 6; .gitignore's comment about non-member examples becomes a case that never occurs.

decisions.question: ADR-001 follow-up on the plugin mechanism: where is nidana_dart_lint enabled so that dart analyze runs its rules?

options.label: Workspace root options, added by the phase that creates the plugin
options.consequence: The rules run over every member, the tree's own packages included; a plugin that does not build fails every root analyze, so every gate depends on the plugin's health.

options.label: nidana_integration's own options
options.consequence: Would scope the rules to the example app, but the analyzer rejects plugins in a member's options (plugins_in_inner_options).

options.label: Recorded invocations only
options.consequence: A broken plugin never fails a member's gate, but no member, the example app included, is ever checked by dart analyze.

options.label: nidana_integration outside the workspace
options.consequence: Its own options may then enable the plugin, but it needs its own resolution and lockfile, path dependencies plus overrides for every package, and gates that resolve twice.

decisions.chosen: Workspace root options, added by the phase that creates the plugin
decisions.why: The analyzer accepts a plugin only in the options at the root of a pub workspace (Q11, and dart.dev's analyzer-plugins page says 'at the root of your package or workspace'). Enabled there, it reports in every member (Q11b); a broken plugin fails analyze with exit 3 (Q11c), which is loud rather than silent. ADR-001's nested fixture options keep it off surface and reject fixtures (Q11d), and recorded invocations still enable it by relative path (contract-fixtures Q19, workspace-layout Q13, Q15). Running the rules over the tree's own packages also checks that they obey Spec §3.1 and §4.4 themselves.

decisions.question: The analysis server resolves a plugin in its own synthetic package outside the workspace, where a hosted constraint on an unpublished sibling fails. Where do the workspace scan and the checks that need nidana_dart_contracts' analyses (root D4) run?

options.label: Command entry of nidana_dart_codegen; nidana_dart_lint depends on no nidana package
options.consequence: The plugin keeps per-library rules only and loads anywhere; the aggregate checks run the model's analyses from a package that already depends on contracts and owns the catalog scan and graph emission.

options.label: nidana_dart_lint with a path dependency on contracts and publish_to: none
options.consequence: Keeps Guide C.2's grouping and loads as a plugin (Q13), but the package is unpublishable until edited, and per-library plugin rules have no use for aggregate analyses.

options.label: A separate scan package
options.consequence: Clearer naming, a ninth package, and the scan shares the catalog scan with the codegen across a package boundary.

decisions.chosen: Command entry of nidana_dart_codegen; nidana_dart_lint depends on no nidana package
decisions.why: Runtime facts: a plugin with a hosted constraint on an unpublished sibling fails to load (Q12); a path dependency loads (Q13) but is an analyzer warning and a publish error in a publishable package (Q11, Q16). Stated reasons for the codegen as host: Spec §3.11 says the single-writer scan feeds the topology graph generator so that they 'share infrastructure', Guide C.3 lists the codegen's topology-graph.json as the CI lint manifest for cycle detection, and root D4 requires the CI checks to call the same analyses activation calls. Plugin rules see one library at a time (OQ-T2's premise), so they need none of those aggregate analyses. Partially resolves OQ-T2; the scan's inputs stay with nidana.tooling. Changes the proposal's 'lint holds the workspace scan'. Signal that would change it: a plugin rule that must run the model's analyses inside the IDE.

decisions.question: How does nidana_dart_lint constrain analyzer and analysis_server_plugin, given that the plugin runs under the synthetic package's resolution while its tests run under the workspace's?

options.label: Exact pins to the lockfile's versions
options.consequence: Both resolutions agree (13.3.0 and 0.3.18); the pins move with the SDK pin, and a published plugin works only with servers that accept 0.3.18.

options.label: Open or caret constraints
options.consequence: The synthetic package resolves analyzer 14.5.0 and analysis_server_plugin 0.3.24 while tests ran on 13.3.0 and 0.3.18: the shipped plugin runs code no test ran.

decisions.chosen: Exact pins to the lockfile's versions
decisions.why: Q14 shows the skew with open constraints; Q15 shows exact pins make the synthetic package resolve the workspace's versions and the plugin load on the pinned SDK, whose server asks for analysis_server_plugin ^0.3.8. analysis_server_plugin itself pins analyzer exactly per release (0.3.24 pins 14.5.0), so the two versions move as a pair anyway. analyzer_testing 0.3.2 resolves beside 13.3.0 for rule tests (Q17).

decisions.question: ADR-001 follow-up: does the codegen's command entry that runs outside build_runner (the file replay of topic-codegen@v1) belong in this ADR or in the codegen contract?

options.label: Package shape here, command interface in the contract
options.consequence: This ADR fixes that nidana_dart_codegen has bin/ command entries over the same pure generator functions as its builders; topic-codegen@v1 and nidana-checks@v1 fix executable names, arguments and outputs.

options.label: Leave all of it to topic-codegen@v1
options.consequence: The contract author decides whether a command exists at all, after the package layout is fixed; nidana-checks@v1's scan command would have no fixed host.

decisions.chosen: Package shape here, command interface in the contract
decisions.why: The ADR says why and the contract says what (hsdd-adr). Whether a package has executables, and that builders and commands share one pure generator, is package shape across two contracts and the integration node; the arguments are an interface. Q8 shows a command entry calling the builder's pure function writes byte-identical output from the workspace root, and Q9 that dart run {package}:{executable} works there.

decisions.question: ADR-001 follow-up: what is nidana_contract_check's full dependency set, given it joins the single resolution?

options.label: args, json_schema, matcher, package_config, path; test as dev
options.consequence: Covers ADR-001's CLI, schema validation, the fixture.dart exports asserting with matcher, and PENDING detection from the package configuration.

options.label: json_schema only
options.consequence: What ADR-001 names, but fixture.dart's matcher-based assertions and the package_config read would add undeclared imports that depend_on_referenced_packages reports.

decisions.chosen: args, json_schema, matcher, package_config, path; test as dev
decisions.why: ADR-001 items 4 and 9: fixture.dart exports ConformanceCase and expectMatchesSchema (json_schema plus matcher), the tool parses --set and --guarantee (args) and tells a PENDING binding from the workspace's package configuration (package_config). All resolve in the full stand-in workspace with Flutter (Q1); a stand-in fixture.dart compiles against them. Matcher is pinned by flutter_test to 0.12.20.

decisions.question: May a published member list test or flutter_test under dependencies (for example the Flutter adapter's widget-test helpers taking a WidgetTester)?

options.label: Neither test nor flutter_test in a published member's dependencies; matcher allowed
options.consequence: The runtime's testing.dart and the adapter's helpers serve VM and widget tests alike; helpers cannot take a WidgetTester, so a test calls tester.pump itself.

options.label: Allow flutter_test in nidana_dart_runtime_flutter
options.consequence: Helpers can extend WidgetTester; every app's main dependency graph then carries flutter_test and its exact pins.

options.label: A separate Flutter test package
options.consequence: WidgetTester helpers without touching the adapter's dependencies, at the cost of a ninth package.

decisions.chosen: Neither test nor flutter_test in a published member's dependencies; matcher allowed
decisions.why: Extends the proposal's 'testing.dart has no dependency on package:test' to the Flutter adapter for symmetry; matcher stays allowed because ADR-001's conformance libraries show it works under both test and testWidgets. Judgement: no experiment shows a helper that needs WidgetTester. Signal that would change it: the flutter-binding@v1 author finds a helper that cannot be written without WidgetTester, which would supersede this item. Recorded in nidana.flutter.md's widget-test library line.

decisions.question: What strictness does the workspace-wide analyze hold?

options.label: Clean under fvm dart analyze --fatal-infos at the root
options.consequence: Lint infos and the plugin's rules, which report at INFO severity, fail analyze; every member is held to the lint set.

options.label: Default dart analyze (warnings and errors fail)
options.consequence: Lint infos and every plugin rule pass silently, so the v1 checks never fail a gate.

decisions.chosen: Clean under fvm dart analyze --fatal-infos at the root
decisions.why: The plugin's warning rules report at INFO severity (Q11b, Q11d, Q13), so without --fatal-infos the v1 checks cannot fail anything. ADR-001's surface fixtures already pass under --fatal-infos.

decisions.question: Which SDK constraint do the members declare?

options.label: ^3.13.0, the Dart of the .fvmrc pin
options.consequence: The bound is what the tree tests; adopters need Dart 3.13 (Flutter 3.47) or later.

options.label: A lower bound such as ^3.11.0
options.consequence: Wider adoption on older Flutter releases, but no gate tests that bound.

decisions.chosen: ^3.13.0, the Dart of the .fvmrc pin
decisions.why: Nothing in the tree tests a lower SDK, and publishing is out of v1 (root D1), so the bound matters only at publication, where widening it is non-breaking. Signal that would change it: an owner-named adopting app pinned to an older Flutter.

decisions.question: How are member versions managed before v1?

options.label: Lockstep from 0.1.0; unpublished members carry no version
options.consequence: One version for every published member; a bump touches every version and inter-member constraint in one change.

options.label: Independent semver per package
options.consequence: Finer releases, but inter-member constraints drift and a one-owner tree gains nothing from independent cadences.

decisions.chosen: Lockstep from 0.1.0; unpublished members carry no version
decisions.why: Kept from the proposal. With hosted sibling constraints, a version that no longer satisfies a sibling's constraint fails resolution (Q3), so lockstep bumps keep the workspace resolving. 0.1.0 is the conventional first pre-release on pub. Signal that would change it: a package with a separate consumer base that needs its own release cadence.

decisions.question: Do published members carry pub metadata files in v1, although publishing is an owner action?

options.label: README, CHANGELOG and a copy of the repository LICENSE in each published member
options.consequence: pub publish --dry-run reports no error, so publication needs only the owner's repository field and credentials.

options.label: Leave metadata to the publishing action
options.consequence: Less to write now; every package then fails publish validation until edited.

decisions.chosen: README, CHANGELOG and a copy of the repository LICENSE in each published member
decisions.why: Q16 shows a missing LICENSE is the only publish error of a member laid out this way; README and CHANGELOG are the remaining recommendations. The repository already carries an Apache-2.0 LICENSE, so no licensing choice is made here. The repository field and publication stay with the owner.

decisions.question: Does the ADR fix library naming inside members, which contract fixtures import by package URI?

options.label: Main library lib/{name}.dart; other public libraries named by their contract; the rest under lib/src/
options.consequence: Fixtures can name main-library URIs now; contracts own the names of extra public libraries such as testing.dart.

options.label: Leave library names to each contract
options.consequence: No rule to break, but nine contract steps choose names without a convention.

decisions.chosen: Main library lib/{name}.dart; other public libraries named by their contract; the rest under lib/src/
decisions.why: ADR-001 fixtures import package:{name}/{library}.dart and ban src/ imports, so every contract needs public library URIs. The main-library convention is pub's default and matches the publish validator's naming check (Q16 flags lib/main.dart only because the plugin requires that name). The plugin's lib/main.dart is the one stated exception, required by the analysis server's synthetic entry point.

decisions.question: Which ids does affects name: the seven nodes of the proposal only, or also the nine contracts?

options.label: Seven nodes and all nine contracts
options.consequence: Every contract file carries Governed by ADR-002, so contract authors see the package names, library rules and the codegen and lint hosts the Interfaces depend on.

options.label: Seven nodes only
options.consequence: Phases still receive the ADR through their nodes, but contract steps would not be pointed at the package and library names their fixtures import.

decisions.chosen: Seven nodes and all nine contracts
decisions.why: Every contract's fixtures import a package URI this ADR fixes, bus-testing@v1 and flutter-binding@v1 are shaped by the test-framework rule, and topic-codegen@v1 and nidana-checks@v1 by the command and plugin hosts. ADR-001 set the same precedent. Contract ids are forward references until their files exist.

decisions.question: OQ-T2 asks where the single-writer workspace scan runs. With item 8 fixing its host, does the row stay OPEN or become PARTIAL?

options.label: PARTIAL, residual: what the scan reads
options.consequence: The row points at ADR-002 for the host and leaves the scan's inputs to nidana.tooling's decomposition.

options.label: Leave OPEN
options.consequence: The tooling decomposition would reopen a host the package layout already fixed.

decisions.chosen: PARTIAL, residual: what the scan reads
decisions.why: The conventions define PARTIAL with the residual under Waits on, and hsdd-adr asks that an ADR resolving an OQ updates its owning spec's row. The three options OQ-T2 lists (analyzer scan, catalog IR plus AST scan, both with IDE surfacing) all remain open and all fit a codegen command.

experiments.question: Does the planned workspace layout hold on the pinned SDK with stand-in members (contracts, runtime, navigation, Flutter adapter, codegen with builder and command entry, analyzer plugin and three plugin variants, replay tool, Flutter integration app): what one resolution yields, how sibling constraints, globs, examples, analysis options, plugin enabling and plugin resolution behave, and whether builders, commands, tests and publish validation work?
experiments.finding: One resolution with Flutter and test holds analyzer 13.3.0, analysis_server_plugin 0.3.18, build 4.0.11, source_gen 4.2.4, build_runner 2.16.1, test 1.31.1 (flutter_test pins test_api 0.7.12, test_core 0.6.18 caps analyzer <14). Hosted sibling constraints resolve locally and mismatches fail; globs work; pub get in a member writes the root lockfile only. A non-member example/ package fails the root pub get (exit 69); nested members work; pubspec-free examples are part of the member. Excludes hide ref/, docs/, hsdd/; members inherit the root lint set and strict modes. A member's options cannot enable a plugin (plugins_in_inner_options); root-enabled, the plugin reports in every member, stays off fixtures under a nested options file, and fails analyze with exit 3 when it does not compile; its rules report at INFO. The plugin runs from a synthetic package outside the workspace: a hosted dependency on an unpublished sibling fails to load (exit 4), a path dependency loads, open constraints resolve analyzer 14.5.0 there against 13.3.0 in the workspace, exact pins align them and load. build_runner runs in the Flutter member; a command over the same pure generator writes identical bytes; dart run package:executable works from the root. Publish dry-run of a hosted-constraint member fails only on LICENSE; a path dependency is a publish error. An outside app needs dependency_overrides for every unpublished sibling. analyzer_testing 0.3.2 resolves beside analyzer 13.3.0.

notes_for_orchestrator: ADR-002 accepted as hsdd/adr/002-package-workspace-layout.md. It keeps the proposal's eight packages and names. Four changes, each forced by docs/auto-run/experiments/workspace-layout/: (1) nidana_dart_lint depends on no nidana package and pins analyzer 13.3.0 and analysis_server_plugin 0.3.18 exactly; (2) the workspace scan and every check over more than one library or the IR run as a command entry of nidana_dart_codegen; (3) the plugin is enabled in the workspace root's analysis_options.yaml, added by the phase that creates nidana_dart_lint; (4) a member's example/ folder has no pubspec. It also adds the root lint set (lints/recommended plus strict modes), the hsdd/** exclude, --fatal-infos as the analyze standard, hosted constraints between members, and the replay tool's full dependency set.

Spec edits beyond the pointer: nidana.md OQ9 detail now cites items 7 and 8 and the 13.3.0 baseline; nidana.tooling.md Owns and Inherited lines reflect the two hosts; OQ-T2 is PARTIAL (residual: what the scan reads); nidana.flutter.md says the widget-test library imports neither flutter_test nor test.

Phase planning, the most important consequence: no phase has yet been told to create the workspace root. The first phase of the tree, nidana.model.1, has to write the root pubspec.yaml (nidana_workspace, explicit workspace list), analysis_options.yaml (item 2, no plugins section yet) and the committed pubspec.lock, alongside packages/nidana_dart_contracts and packages/nidana_contract_check. Every later phase that creates a member adds it to the root workspace list. Parallel member-creating phases therefore collide textually on the root pubspec.yaml and lockfile and need Collides with entries.

Contract steps (S06 to S14): every contract adds Governed by: [ADR-001, ADR-002]. Fixtures import main libraries as package:{name}/{name}.dart; other public libraries (the runtime's testing.dart, any adapter test library) are named by the contract that declares them.

bus-testing@v1 and flutter-binding@v1: the testing libraries import neither test nor flutter_test; matcher is allowed. That bounds OQ-R2's assertion API (matchers are possible; test-framework helpers are not) and means the Flutter widget-test helpers cannot take a WidgetTester. If the flutter-binding@v1 author finds a helper that needs WidgetTester, item 4 needs superseding; flag it rather than working around it.

topic-codegen@v1: name the generator executable of nidana_dart_codegen (fvm dart run nidana_dart_codegen:{executable} {input} {output}) in Validation. Builders and the command call the same pure functions.

nidana-checks@v1: two hosts. Per-library rules come from the plugin under dart analyze; they report at INFO severity, so recorded invocations should run analyze with --fatal-infos, or use --format=machine and record exit 0. Aggregate checks come from the nidana_dart_codegen scan command. In a recorded invocation, files/analysis_options.yaml enables the plugin by relative path. Seeded violations can never live in a member's analyzed code.

nidana.tooling decomposition: plugin rules are the per-library v1 checks (raw-string topic use, global bus accessor, sensitive flag warning). The codegen command holds topic name uniqueness across registries, single-writer, inter-topology cycles, intra-topology self-reference and scope compatibility. The rules also run over the tree's own packages, so they must accept topic declarations. The resolution gives build 4.0.11, source_gen 4.2.4, build_runner 2.16.1 and analyzer 13.3.0, with analyzer_testing 0.3.2 for rule tests. build_runner 2.16.1 dropped --delete-conflicting-outputs (Q7 warning). The plugin must build at every merge, or every gate that analyzes fails.
nidana.integration: build_runner runs inside packages/nidana_integration. The CI slice's seeded violations go in excluded trees analyzed by explicit path, or are passed as input to the scan command.
